policy.acceptable: Optional dependency probes, logging, cleanup, or shell-only formatting paths may keep a broad catch when the fallback is explicit and does not change trust-critical verdicts.
policy.questionable: Active paths that coerce config, pair data, or shape user-visible outputs need a narrower catch or stronger justification before they should remain broad.
policy.should_remove: Trust-critical determinism, guard evidence, guard execution, and pairing logic must not rely on blanket catches because they can hide correctness gaps or downgrade fail-closed behavior.

entries.rationale: Phase-shell wrappers preserve buffered child output, normalize CLI exit codes, and isolate heterogeneous failures while orchestration and report-contract helpers still raise mixed exception types.
Receipt-bound selection finalizers are extension boundaries with heterogeneous failures; both catches terminate report publication through the explicit fail callback.
Best-effort runtime quantization observation is non-authoritative for ordinary runs; strict evidence verification separately requires and validates the proof sidecar.
Optional third-party runtime introspection converts arbitrary proxy and module failures into an explicit unobserved result that downstream assurance checks reject.
Optional backend configuration introspection resolves only ambiguous live wrapper families; any exception returns no family and therefore fails proof recognition closed.
